catalogue_claim.text: Resolves the Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions and the Hausdorff-dimension conjecture in four. In three dimensions, the radius-δ tube maximal operator maps \(L^3(\mathbb R^3)\) to \(L^3(S^2)\) with norm \(O_\varepsilon(\delta^{-\varepsilon})\) for every ε > 0. In four dimensions, every set containing a unit segment in every direction has Hausdorff dimension four.

efforts.name: Updates: Sharing AI progress on mathematics (amazing!); and my lecture plans
efforts.summary: Kalai calls the release an amazing milestone for mathematics, with three caveats: results sit at different stages of verification, Lean verification may itself have issues, and other AI-derived results they did not collect (for example irrationality of zeta(5), Komlos, Chvatal, KLS) exist.

efforts.name: Mathematicians React With Shock And Wonder After OpenAI Releases Over 300 Math Proofs At Once
efforts.summary: Collects first-day reactions posted on X: Kontorovich on the quasi-RH Fields Medal remark, Strogatz on the matrix-multiplication leap, Lozano-Robledo's staggering-scale remark, Ivanisvili on four-dimensional Kakeya, Alpoge, Litt, Bloom's advice to take a holiday, Porto, Kogler, Sinha and Armstrong.

efforts.name: The most interesting mathematical discoveries in OpenAI's 722 new papers
efforts.summary: Round-up of the most notable claims: quasi-Riemann hypothesis, partial versions of the Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer and Hodge conjectures, four-dimensional Kakeya, a tiny speed-up for integer multiplication and Fourier transforms, and a claim that the plane cannot be five-coloured.

efforts.name: The most exciting claims from OpenAI's heap of new proofs
efforts.summary: Walks through the headline claims by field with named specialists commenting: quasi-Riemann hypothesis and Siegel zeros, Hilbert's tenth problem over the rationals, four-dimensional Kakeya, a sigma-model analogue of Yang-Mills, matrix multiplication at 9/4, L = RL = BPL, the Unique Games Conjecture, unitary synthesis.

efforts.name: 'Pure insanity': Mathematicians will need years to make sense of OpenAI's latest drop
efforts.summary: Survey of more than three dozen mathematicians: awe mixed with anxiety, difficulty reading the papers, uneven formalisation, concerns about thin attribution and short bibliographies, reports of research programmes made redundant, and a view that OpenAI followed some but not all of AGMAI's recommendations.
efforts.traction: part of The Verge collection "All the drama around AI's takeover of mathematics"

efforts.name: What the Machine Invented: Mining New Mathematical Instruments from OpenAI's October 2026 Release (arXiv 2610.17090)
efforts.summary: A survey of 38 families that extracts the new lemmas, constructions and proof mechanisms in each source argument, with antecedents, caveats and a formalisation scoreboard; it says Claude Fable 5.1 did the initial extraction, that novelty verdicts are provisional, and that no Lean was compiled.
